analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: MO' BOUNCE
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +58bps at 7,757 with a $400mm market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX +113bps at 29,822, R2K +36bps at 2,783, Dow +69bps at 52,857. Volume was 15.887bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.532bn.
The market was lifted by momentum and chasing in high-velocity pockets, including more than 1m SPCX call options traded.

Mag7 lagged. The desk (Bartlett) attributes this to competition concerns after SPCX SI results, rotation into SPCX, Cleveland checks weighing on GOOGL, and possible source-of-funds trading ahead of expected future issuance.

Semis bounced but the move felt underwhelming after 10 of the last 11 sessions lower, despite positive news flow and constructive overnight global tech price action (SMCI +10% on a positive pre-announcement).
Desk activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale. The floor finished +3% better to buy on still relatively muted notional.

Asset manager flows were roughly flat, with demand in Financials/REITs, industrials and energy and supply in utilities, healthcare and tech. Hedge funds were small net buyers, with demand in tech, healthcare and financials and supply in communication services.
After the bell: META +5% on a Q3 revenue beat and Q4 guidance of $73-76bn vs $73.57bn consensus. A new class of stock is coming in Jan 2027.
After the bell: TSLA +4%. Q3 deliveries were a clear beat but that news came in early October. Qualitative commentary seemed more positive than in recent quarters.
After the bell: LRCX -7.5% despite a quarterly beat. F2Q gross margin guide 52.4% vs consensus of about 52%, and guidance slightly above the Street.
After the bell: IBM +6% (was +4% into the print). Software revenue accelerated to +9% y/y constant currency from +5% last quarter, with a rebound in Transaction Processing revenue.

Derivatives: a quiet day on the vol desk after VIX expiry, with the Street cleaner coming out of the print. Index vol rose across the whole term structure while skew compressed steadily through the session.

Fixed-strike vol was bid on the move higher, which the desk had not seen in a while. Buyers of short-dated upside appeared in real size, with $18m of premium spent on SPY Nov 800 calls and Dec 810 calls.
With positioning increasingly defensive, the desk views right-tail hedges as historically cheap. The S&P is about 1.1% below its Oct 6 peak. The S&P implied move for the rest of the week is 78bps.

Hedge funds have heavily net sold global equities in October, with short sales outpacing long buys by about 5 to 1. Long leverage is at the 73rd percentile of the past year (94th percentile over 5 years). Short leverage has risen sharply and is near 5-year highs (99th percentile).
